title: Isolated trace ID translation and ingest-tiering for private deployments
creator: Alex Kim
description:
Problem: For Private and Dedicated deployments we currently forward traces and logs through shared ingress collectors, which risks accidental leakage of tenant identifiers and makes it hard to apply different retention/processing policies per deployment. We need a solution that: (1) preserves linkability of traces across services owned by the same customer, (2) prevents tenant-identifying values from entering multi-tenant shared pipelines, and (3) enables tiered ingest (hot path for latency/error signals, cold path for verbose logs) without adding noticeable latency to request paths.

Proposed solution: Implement a two-part system: (A) a short-lived Trace ID Translation service that runs on the perimeter collector in private/Dedicated deployments. It replaces tenant-visible trace IDs with internal ephemeral IDs before forwarding to the shared pipeline and maintains a local mapping store for correlation. The mapping keys are rotated and encrypted with tenant-scoped KMS keys. (B) Ingest-tiering policy enforced at the perimeter collector: sampling and routing rules classify telemetry into HOT (error/latency traces + metrics), WARM (sparse traces, key logs), and COLD (debug logs, verbose spans). HOT is forwarded to low-latency hot-path collectors and retained at higher resolution; COLD is routed to cold storage with shard-compression.

Goals: preserve cross-service trace correlation for a tenant, ensure no tenant-identifying fields escape the boundary, allow per-deployment retention and cost controls, and keep additional p99 latency on the request path < 5ms.

Out of scope: changes to hosted shared pipeline storage format, global re-indexing of historical traces.
acceptance_criteria: Perimeter collector replaces tenant-facing trace IDs with ephemeral internal IDs and forwards transformed payloads to shared pipeline
Mapping store is encrypted and rotates keys per deployment; mapping lifetime configurable (default 12 hours)
SDK tracing hooks include a new 'deployment-signed' header and graceful fallback when header absent
Ingest-tiering policy routes HOT telemetry to low-latency collectors and COLD telemetry to low-cost cold storage with >10x lower retention cost
End-to-end p99 added latency from perimeter translation + routing < 5ms for 99% of requests in lab microbenchmarks
Security review completed and Confluence threat model updated with mitigation details
Dashboard surfaces: per-deployment hot/cold volume, mapped trace collisions, translation error rate, and ingestion latency percentiles
tasks: Design perimeter Trace ID translation API and encryption scheme (Priya + Sam) - design doc: https://confluence.redwood.local/display/OBS/Trace+ID+Translation
Implement translation logic in perimeter collector (Go) - branch: github.com/redwood/collector/tree/eng/trace-translate (PR #4128)
Add SDK tracing hook and header support to runtime SDKs (Python/Go/Node) - RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RB-obs-trace-hooks
Implement ingest-tiering rules engine and config UI for Console (frontend + backend)
Add integration tests for mapping rotation and offline recovery
Run security review and KMS integration test with Private deployment staging cluster
Create dashboards and alerts in Console: /dashboards/private-observability/trace-translation
notes: 10% design alternative considered: HMACing tenant id into trace id instead of translation. Rejected due to leakability and inability to revoke without re-issuing traces.
Mapping store will be a local RocksDB with AES-GCM field encryption; we will expose size and eviction metrics to avoid unbounded growth.
Edge case: cross-deployment customer setups (multiple Dedicated clusters) will require an optional global mapping handshake; scope for a follow-up ticket.
Perf run (03/05/2026): translation adds median 0.6ms, p99 3.9ms on m5.large-like instance with 1000 rps synthetic load. Details: https://perf.redwood.internal/reports/trace-translate-20260305
Initial security review notes: ensure header is signed and timestamped to prevent replay; incorporate nonce per mapping entry. Assigned to Security: Jordan Lee.
Related customer ask: AcmeCloud requested per-deployment 90-day retention for HOT traces. Evaluate cost delta as part of release planning.
